title: Declare the daemon context dependency
description: Prerequisite for task-203a5ca7aada4375a98a95df8773e249. Fresh measurement at HEAD 15918c7: @moe/context is a real workspace package and its root exports selectContext/renderContext/digestContextManifest, but apps/daemon declares no dependency, its pnpm-lock importer has no link, and a plain-Node bare import from apps/daemon fails ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Land only the dependency edge and prove it resolves.
definitionOfDone: apps/daemon/package.json declares `@moe/context: workspace:*` in dependencies and pnpm-lock.yaml records the apps/daemon importer link to `../../packages/context`; no unrelated importer changes are introduced.

A compiled temporary probe inside apps/daemon imports `selectContext`, `renderContext`, `digestContextManifest`, and their public types from the bare `@moe/context` specifier and typechecks exit 0; the probe is deleted in the same command.
A plain-Node bare-root import from apps/daemon resolves the three production functions at runtime, while a negative deep-import probe remains refused by package exports.

Daemon and context typecheck/test commands execute separately with nonzero test-count output, and completion names the remaining context-manifest children of task-203a5ca7aada4375a98a95df8773e249 as consumers.
taskRails: Own only apps/daemon/package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml; do not edit @moe/context sources or add a production call site in this plumbing task.
Use pnpm workspace install/update semantics and inspect the importer diff; do not hand-edit unrelated lockfile sections.
No deep imports, tsconfig paths, project references, scratch probe residue, or vacuous filter passes; explicit owned-path commit only.

implementationPlan.description: RE-CONFIRM THE EDGE IS STILL LANDED, then change nothing. The architect measured this task COMPLETE-ON-ARRIVAL at HEAD a42ae2f (see the task comment for the full transcript): `apps/daemon/package.json` already declares `@moe/context`, and `pnpm-lock.yaml:107-110` already carries `'@moe/context': {specifier: workspace:*, version: link:../../packages/context}` inside the `apps/daemon:` importer. The description's contrary measurement was taken at HEAD 15918c7 and is stale. Re-run both checks — `node -e "console.log('@moe/context' in require('./apps/daemon/package.json').dependencies)"` and `grep -n "packages/context" pnpm-lock.yaml` — and confirm they still hold. IF THEY DO: make NO edit to either file, run NO `pnpm install`, and commit NEITHER path. Re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate, and a needless lockfile churn in a shared worktree is a real hazard rather than a harmless no-op. IF THEY DO NOT hold — meaning a peer reverted the edge between planning and execution — stop and report rather than silently switching into build mode; that is a different task than the one planned here.

Reproduce the two probes as recorded EVIDENCE, deleting every probe in the command that creates it. (a) COMPILED: write `apps/daemon/src/__ctx-probe.ts` importing `selectContext`, `renderContext`, `digestContextManifest` and their public types from the bare `@moe/context` specifier, run `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`, require ZERO diagnostics naming the probe file, and `rm` it in the same command; confirm with `git status --porcelain -- apps/daemon/src` that nothing survives. DO NOT substitute a grep: `packages/context/src/index.ts` is five `export *` lines, so a barrel grep for the three symbol names returns nothing and proves neither presence nor absence. (b) RUNTIME, from a working directory inside `apps/daemon`, plain Node with NO loader flag — the export target is `./src/index.ts` and Node 24 strips types natively, the same reason the daemon's own start script is `node ./src/daemon-main.ts`: `import('@moe/context')` must report all three as `function`, and the NEGATIVE control `import('@moe/context/src/context-render.js')` must reject with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`, since the exports map is `{".": "./src/index.ts"}` and maps no subpaths. Run the runtime probes from PowerShell, not the Bash tool — a prior plain-Node smoke on this repo failed only because Git Bash rewrote paths. Record both transcripts verbatim; the negative control is what stops the positive one from passing vacuously.

Run the gates separately and record the consumers, which is the only DoD item not already satisfied. Four legs, exit codes captured INDIVIDUALLY rather than `&&`-chained: `pnpm --filter @moe/context typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/context test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`. Both package names resolve (`@moe/context` is packages/context, `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, each declaring both scripts — verified at plan time). DoD 4 demands NONZERO test-count output, and rail 3 forbids a vacuous filter pass: `pnpm --filter <pkg> <script>` prints "No projects matched the filters" and EXITS 0 for a package absent from the workspace, so record the `Test Files N passed` line for each test leg and treat a leg with no count line as UNVERIFIED, not as passing. The daemon suite can be red at baseline from foreign in-flight slices — this task owns no source, so any red is by definition foreign: attribute it with the merge-base-versus-HEAD failing-path delta, disclose it verbatim with exact failing lines, and do not fabricate green. Finally name the remaining context-manifest children of task-203a5ca7aada4375a98a95df8773e249 as the consumers in the completion evidence, as DoD 4 requires — this task deliberately lands no call site, so the consumers must be named rather than implied. Expect NO commit: a finished task with no diff is a legitimate outcome here and is not a missing-evidence problem.

comments.content:
MEASUREMENT: this task is COMPLETE-ON-ARRIVAL. architect-77071474 at HEAD a42ae2f. The description's measurement was taken at HEAD 15918c7; the edge has landed since, so the gap it names is closed and there is nothing to build.

**DoD 1 — SATISFIED.** `apps/daemon/package.json` declares `@moe/context` in dependencies, and `pnpm-lock.yaml:107-110` carries the apps/daemon importer entry:
```
  apps/daemon:
    dependencies:
      '@moe/context':
        specifier: workspace:*
        version: link:../../packages/context
```

**DoD 2 — SATISFIED, verified by compiled probe.** A temporary `apps/daemon/src/__ctx-probe.ts` importing `selectContext`, `renderContext` and `digestContextManifest` from the bare `@moe/context` specifier typechecks with ZERO diagnostics under `npx tsc --project apps/daemon/tsconfig.json --noEmit`. Probe deleted in the same command; `git status` confirms no residue.

Note for anyone re-checking: `packages/context/src/index.ts` is FIVE `export *` lines (context-contract, context-render, context-selection, dead-end-journal, release-handoff). A root-barrel grep for the three symbol names returns NOTHING and is not evidence either way — probe, do not grep.

**DoD 3 — SATISFIED, both halves, run from apps/daemon under plain Node v24.16.0 with no flags:**
- `import('@moe/context')` → `BARE_OK function function function` — all three production functions resolve at runtime.
- `import('@moe/context/src/context-render.js')` → `DEEP_REFUSED_GOOD ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` — the deep path is refused by the package exports map, which is `{".": "./src/index.ts"}` and maps no subpaths.

Runtime resolution works with no loader flag because the export target is a `.ts` file and Node 24 strips types natively — the same reason `node ./src/daemon-main.ts` is the daemon's own start script.

**DoD 4 — the only part left**: run the daemon and context gates separately with nonzero test counts, and name the remaining context-manifest children of task-203a5ca7 as consumers. Plan submitted covers exactly that and nothing more.

Per the stale-by-default rail: re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner in a shared worktree. There is no manifest edit and no `pnpm install` to run here — a needless lock churn would be a real hazard, not a no-op.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
PLANNING VERIFICATION ONLY, BECAUSE THE WORK IS ALREADY DONE. The obvious plan — edit the manifest, run `pnpm install`, prove the edge — would re-do an edge that is already committed. The stale-by-default rail names this exact failure: "GAP CLAIMED PRESENT, actually closed ... re-implementing a landed surface is a silent duplicate that collides with its owner in a shared worktree, and it wastes the same context load as the opposite error." So the plan is three verification steps and an explicit instruction to change nothing.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: `moe.report_blocked`. Nothing blocks this task; it is finished except for its gates. Blocking would park a CRITICAL prerequisite of the Foundation context-manifest chain for no reason.

CONSIDERED AND REJECTED: asking a governor to close it administratively. DoD 4 still requires the gates to run with nonzero counts and the consumers to be named, and that evidence should be produced by the normal worker/QA path rather than asserted by an architect. Running it as a three-step task also leaves a durable record of WHY no diff exists, which a silent administrative close would not.

A NO-DIFF COMPLETION IS THE EXPECTED OUTCOME and is called out in the final step so neither the worker nor QA reads the absent commit as missing evidence.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
MEASURED AND PROBED AT HEAD a42ae2f. The description's measurement is from HEAD 15918c7 and is stale in the GAP-CLOSED direction.

DoD 1 ALREADY TRUE. `apps/daemon/package.json` declares `@moe/context`. `pnpm-lock.yaml` lines 107-110 hold the apps/daemon importer entry `'@moe/context': {specifier: workspace:*, version: link:../../packages/context}`, alphabetically first in that block — `@moe/import` is now present in the same block too, so the sibling importer task landed as well.

DoD 2 ALREADY TRUE, PROVEN BY COMPILED PROBE. A temporary probe in apps/daemon importing `selectContext`, `renderContext` and `digestContextManifest` from the bare specifier produced ZERO tsc diagnostics; probe deleted in the same command.

A GREP WOULD HAVE LIED HERE. `packages/context/src/index.ts` is exactly five lines, all `export *` — from ./context-contract.js, ./context-render.js, ./context-selection.js, ./dead-end-journal.js and ./release-handoff.js. `grep selectContext packages/context/src/index.ts` returns NOTHING while the symbol is genuinely exported. Root-barrel greps are blind to star re-exports; only a probe settles it.

DoD 3 ALREADY TRUE, BOTH HALVES, PROBED UNDER PLAIN NODE v24.16.0 FROM apps/daemon WITH NO FLAGS. Bare root import reported `BARE_OK function function function`. The negative deep-import control `@moe/context/src/context-render.js` rejected with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED`. That refusal is structural: `packages/context/package.json` sets `exports: {".": "./src/index.ts"}` and maps no subpaths, so every deep path is blocked by Node's exports resolution rather than by convention.

WHY RUNTIME RESOLUTION NEEDS NO LOADER. The export target is a `.ts` file and Node 24 strips types natively; this repo already depends on that, since apps/daemon's own `start` script is `node ./src/daemon-main.ts`. If an implementer finds themselves reaching for a flag, something else is wrong — the flag would be hiding a failure rather than fixing one.

GATES RESOLVE BY NAME: `@moe/context` is packages/context and `@moe/daemon` is apps/daemon, each declaring `typecheck` and `test`.
planningNotes.risks:
1. THE LARGEST RISK IS A WORKER WHO FOLLOWS THE DESCRIPTION INSTEAD OF THE PLAN. It states plainly that the dependency is absent and a plain-Node import fails ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND. That was true at HEAD 15918c7 and is false now. Acting on it means running `pnpm install` against an already-correct lock and committing churn nobody asked for, in a worktree shared with other agents.
2. DO NOT SUBSTITUTE A GREP FOR THE PROBE. index.ts is five `export *` lines; a grep for the three symbols returns nothing while all three resolve. Reading that silence as absence would flip this task straight back into a duplicate build.
3. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL IS NOT OPTIONAL. Without the deep-import refusal, the positive bare import proves only that SOMETHING resolved. Assert the exact `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` code, not merely that the deep import rejected — a typo in the path also rejects, with a different code.
4. RUN THE RUNTIME PROBES FROM POWERSHELL. A prior plain-Node smoke on this repo failed purely because Git Bash rewrote paths, and that failure looks exactly like a genuine resolution failure.
5. EXPECT NO COMMIT, AND DO NOT MANUFACTURE ONE. There is nothing to stage. An empty commit to "claim" the task, or a whitespace edit to produce a diff, would be worse than the absent commit it is trying to explain.
6. If a peer reverts the edge between planning and execution, that is a genuinely different task — stop and report rather than quietly switching into build mode under a plan that says change nothing.
